title: R’ Yonatan or Natan of Beit Gubrin
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: R’ Yonatan (and sometimes R’ Natan) of Bei Gubrin.
In Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot, chapter 1, END of halakhah 1, R’ Avin bar Bisna transmits in his name; and in Shemot Rabbah, end of section 44, R’ Acha transmits in his name.
Rabbi Simon reports in his name in Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 7:3 and in Shir HaShirim Rabbah, at Hyman’s printed locator פ״ד־פ״ד.
And Kohelet Rabbah 3:2 reads R’ Natan of Bei Gubrin. There, at 5:10, Hyman says “R’ Yonatan in his name” is an error and SHOULD READ R’ Simon.
And Vayikra Rabbah 17:5 has R’ Yaakov in the name of R’ Yehudah in the name of R’ Natan of Bei Gubrin.
Tanchuma, Toledot 23, has R’ Abba speaking in R’ Yochanan ד״ג [contextually of Beit Gubrin]’s name; Hyman says WITHOUT DOUBT it SHOULD READ R’ Yonatan.
And in Pesikta Rabbati, parashat Ki Tisa, at Hyman’s locator 66: thus R’ Yonatan of Bei Gubrin began.

notes.text: The supplied Shir HaShirim Rabbah locator is 4–84, not simply verse 4. The changes from Yonatan to Simon and from Yohanan to Yonatan are Hyman’s proposed corrections.

The whole saved Venice Yoma 7:3 scalar 3 explicitly names full Rabbi Simon in full Rabbi Yonatan of Beit Gubrin’s name. This supports those exact local occurrences, not all title occurrences elsewhere in the article. The Yevamot locator is END halakhah 1, omitted from the previous English. Supplied פ״ד־פ״ד remains visible beside the contextual 4–84 reading; the Shir HaShirim location was not inspected and is not reduced to verse 4. Uninspected personal titles remain R-prime, including both heading alternatives. The Kohelet Yonatan-to-Simon correction is Hyman’s SHOULD READ claim; the Tanchuma Yohanan-to-Yonatan correction retains WITHOUT DOUBT SHOULD READ force. ד״ג is a contextual Beit Gubrin expansion, not a proved place identity. Pesikta’s 66 and the complete Yaakov>Yehudah>Natan chain remain.

The consulted Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:4:4 has Rabbi Simon reporting Rabbi Yonatan of Beit Gubrin, as does the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 7:3. Hyman prints פ״ד־פ״ד. In Yevamot 1:1:24 the name of the transmitter is Abun bar Bisna, while the supplied wording has Avin. The end of Shemot Rabbah 44 has Rav Acha reporting Rabbi Yonatan. Kohelet Rabbah 3:2 has Rabbi Simon in Rabbi Natan of Beit Gubrin’s name, while 5:10 has Rabbi Yonatan in Rabbi Yonatan of Beit Gubrin’s name. Vayikra Rabbah 17:5 gives Yaakov, Yehudah, and Natan in that order. Tanchuma Buber, Toldot 23, explicitly has Yochanan of Beit Gubrin, the name Hyman would emend. The consulted Pesikta Rabbati 10 (Ki Tisa) has the opening attributed to Yonatan of Beit Gubrin. It does not establish Hyman’s numbering.
